title: Forming passive sentences: verb + -ing or to-infinitive

sections.title: Active patterns with verb + -ing
sections.content:
Verbs followed by object + -ing in the active are made passive with 'be' + past participle + -ing:
• They saw the monkey climbing over the fence. (= active)
• The monkey was seen climbing over the fence. (= passive)
Also: bring, catch, hear, find, keep, leave, notice, observe, send, show.

sections.title: Verbs followed by being + past participle
sections.content:
Some verbs that can be followed by an -ing form can be used with a passive form being + past participle:
• I really love being given presents.
• The children enjoyed being taken to the zoo.
Also: avoid, deny, describe, dislike, face, hate, (not) imagine, like, remember, report, resent.

sections.title: Verbs with object consisting of a noun phrase and -ing clause
sections.content:
Verbs which in the active are followed by an object consisting of a noun phrase and -ing clause usually have no passive:
• I dread him (or his) finding out. (but not He is dreaded finding out)
Also: anticipate, appreciate, dislike, forget, hate, imagine, like, (not) mind, recall, remember.

sections.title: Active patterns with verb + to-infinitive
sections.content:
The active pattern verb + object + to-infinitive is made passive with 'be' + past participle + to-infinitive. Compare:
• Mr Wang has taught Peter to sing for years. and
• Peter has been taught to sing (by Mr Wang) for years.
Also: advise, allow, ask, believe, consider, expect, feel, instruct, mean, order, require, tell, understand.
Note that in some contexts it is possible to make both verbs passive:
• Changes to the taxation system are expected to be proposed. (compare the active We expect the government to propose changes to the taxation system.)
Some verbs followed by an object + to-infinitive in the active have no passive:
Also: (can't) bear, hate, love, need, prefer, want, wish (= 'liking' and 'wanting' verbs).

sections.title: Active pattern verb + to-infinitive + object
sections.content:
The active pattern verb + to-infinitive + object is made passive with verb + to be + past participle. Compare:
• Supermarkets started to sell fresh pasta only in the 1990s. and
• Fresh pasta started to be sold by supermarkets only in the 1990s.
Some verbs have corresponding meanings in the active and passive. Compare:
• People have come to see organic food as something only the wealthy eat. (active) corresponds to
• Organic food has come to be seen as something only the wealthy eat. (passive)
Also: appear, begin, continue, seem, start, tend.
The meaning of some other verbs does not correspond. Compare:
• Petra wanted to help me. (active) does not correspond to
• I wanted to be helped by Petra. (passive)
Also: agree, aim, arrange, attempt, hope, refuse.

exercises.question: Inger ___ for over three hours when she went for her dental appointment. (keep - wait)
options: was kept waiting
was keeping waiting
kept waiting
has been kept waiting
exercises.explanation:
Answer: was kept waiting
Passive: was + past participle + -ing. Choose the passive form that matches the tense and aspect of the active version.

exercises.question: When the police first questioned him, Wayne ___ in the robbery. (deny - involve)
options: denied being involved
denied to be involved
was denied involving
denied involved
exercises.hint: Passive form of -ing form: being + past participle.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: denied being involved
Passive form of -ing form: being + past participle. Choose the passive form that matches the tense and aspect of the active version.

exercises.question: I ___ the baby while Karen went to answer the door. (observe - hide)
options: was observed hiding
observed hiding
was observing hiding
observed being hidden
exercises.explanation:
Answer: was observed hiding
Passive: was observed -ing. Choose the passive form that matches the tense and aspect of the active version.

exercises.sentence: She is believed to being one of the most talented scientists of her generation.
exercises.correction: She is believed to be one of the most talented scientists of her generation.
exercises.hint: Passive + to-infinitive: is believed to BE (not 'to being').
exercises.explanation:
Answer: is believed to be
The construction 'be + believed/thought/said/reported/known + to-infinitive' uses a plain to-infinitive: 'to be', 'to have', 'to work'. 'To being' is never correct in standard English — the -ing form here is wrong.

exercises.question: When I woke up in hospital, I ___ by the snake but nothing after that. (remember - bite)
options: remembered being bitten
remembered to be bitten
was remembered biting
remembered bitten
exercises.hint: Passive form of -ing: being + past participle.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: remembered being bitten
Passive form of -ing: being + past participle. Choose the passive form that matches the tense and aspect of the active version.

exercises.question: The man ___ a suspicious package under a seat in the train. (find - wander)
options: was found wandering
found wandering
was finding wandering
was found to wander
exercises.explanation:
Answer: was found wandering
Passive: was found + -ing. Choose the passive form that matches the tense and aspect of the active version.

exercises.question: Two teenagers yesterday ___ from school after they were found with over a hundred stolen mobile phones. (face - expel)
options: faced being expelled
faced to be expelled
were faced expelling
faced expelling
exercises.hint: Passive form of -ing: being + past participle.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: faced being expelled
Passive form of -ing: being + past participle. Choose the passive form that matches the tense and aspect of the active version.

exercises.sentence: The company is reported to have making significant losses this year.
exercises.correction: The company is reported to have made significant losses this year.
exercises.hint: For past reference: be + reported + to have + PAST PARTICIPLE (not -ing).
exercises.explanation:
Answer: is reported to have made
For events before the time of reporting, use: be + reported/said/believed + to HAVE + past participle. 'To have made' = the making happened before the reporting. 'To have making' confusingly mixes the infinitive with a gerund — incorrect.

exercises.question: We were asked to show our passports at the border. (active: They asked me to wait.)
options: We were asked to show our passports at the border.
We were ask to show our passports at the border.
We were being asked to show our passports at the border.
We asked to show our passports at the border.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: We were asked to show our passports at the border.
Passive: were asked to show. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.question: They could hear Emil and Laura shouting at each other next door. (Start: Emil and Laura...)
options: Emil and Laura could be heard shouting at each other next door.
Emil and Laura could hear shouting at each other next door.
Emil and Laura were heard shouting at each other next door.
Emil and Laura could being heard shouting at each other next door.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: Emil and Laura could be heard shouting at each other next door.
Passive: could be heard + -ing. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.question: They saw the burglar getting into the museum through a window. (Start: The burglar...)
options: The burglar was seen getting into the museum through a window.
The burglar saw getting into the museum through a window.
The burglar was seen to get into the museum through a window.
The burglar being seen getting into the museum through a window.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: The burglar was seen getting into the museum through a window.
Passive: was seen + -ing. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

exercises.question: The exhibit is said ___ (attract) over two million visitors since it opened.
exercises.hint: Event happened before 'now' → to have + past participle.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: to have attracted
'Is said to have + past participle' describes an event that occurred before the present moment. Compare: 'is said to attract' (currently attracts) vs 'is said to have attracted' (attracted in a completed period up to now).

exercises.question: Kay's questions began to irritate Marco. (Start: Marco...)
options: Marco began to be irritated by Kay's questions.
Marco began being irritated by Kay's questions.
Marco began to irritate by Kay's questions.
Marco was began to be irritated by Kay's questions.
exercises.hint: Passive: began to be + past participle.
exercises.explanation:
Answer: Marco began to be irritated by Kay's questions.
Passive: began to be + past participle. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

Omar was hoped to be selected by the team captain.

Answer: Omar hopes to be selected by the team captain.
Passive: hopes to be + past participle. The grammatical signals in this sentence — the key words, connectors, or context — require this specific form. Look for these signals to make the same choice independently.

options: Holidaymakers continue to be attracted to the south coast.
Holidaymakers continues being attracted to the south coast.

Holidaymakers continue to attract to the south coast.
